# odoo-work-cli completion

## NAME

odoo-work-cli-completion - Generate the autocompletion script for the specified shell

## SYNOPSIS

```text
odoo-work-cli completion bash [--no-descriptions]
odoo-work-cli completion fish [--no-descriptions]
odoo-work-cli completion powershell [--no-descriptions]
odoo-work-cli completion zsh [--no-descriptions]
```

## DESCRIPTION

Print the shell completion script of odoo-work-cli for bash, zsh, fish
or PowerShell on standard output. It completes commands and flags.

The Homebrew cask installs the scripts for bash, zsh and fish; the
release archives contain them in completions/. Load a script by hand as
shown for each shell below.

### bash

Generate the autocompletion script for the bash shell.

This script depends on the 'bash-completion' package.
If it is not installed already, you can install it via your OS's package manager.

To load completions in your current shell session:

```text
source <(odoo-work-cli completion bash)
```

To load completions for every new session, execute once:

#### Linux:

```text
odoo-work-cli completion bash > /etc/bash_completion.d/odoo-work-cli
```

#### macOS:

```text
odoo-work-cli completion bash > $(brew --prefix)/etc/bash_completion.d/odoo-work-cli
```

You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.

### fish

Generate the autocompletion script for the fish shell.

To load completions in your current shell session:

```text
odoo-work-cli completion fish | source
```

To load completions for every new session, execute once:

```text
odoo-work-cli completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/odoo-work-cli.fish
```

You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.

### powershell

Generate the autocompletion script for powershell.

To load completions in your current shell session:

```text
odoo-work-cli completion powershell | Out-String | Invoke-Expression
```

To load completions for every new session, add the output of the above command
to your powershell profile.

### zsh

Generate the autocompletion script for the zsh shell.

If shell completion is not already enabled in your environment you will need
to enable it.  You can execute the following once:

```text
echo "autoload -U compinit; compinit" >> ~/.zshrc
```

To load completions in your current shell session:

```text
source <(odoo-work-cli completion zsh)
```

To load completions for every new session, execute once:

#### Linux:

```text
odoo-work-cli completion zsh > "${fpath[1]}/_odoo-work-cli"
```

#### macOS:

```text
odoo-work-cli completion zsh > $(brew --prefix)/share/zsh/site-functions/_odoo-work-cli
```

You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.

## OPTIONS

`--no-descriptions`
:   Disable completion descriptions.

    *flag; optional*

## GLOBAL OPTIONS

`--backend` *BACKEND*
:   BACKEND: odoo or fake (offline, made-up data; env ODOO_WORK_CLI_BACKEND).

    *string; optional; default: odoo; env: ODOO_WORK_CLI_BACKEND*

`--config` *FILE*
:   Read only the config FILE (skip discovery).

    *string; optional*

`-h`, `--help`
:   Print the help of the command and exit.

## EXIT STATUS

0 on success, 1 on any error, including usage errors. The error is printed as "Error: TEXT" on standard error.

Error kinds this command can fail with:

`validation`
:   Invalid input: unknown flag, bad argument, malformed date, time or hours, a time in the future, an unknown project.

`internal`
:   Anything else: an unexpected Odoo response or a bug.

## EXAMPLES

Load completion into the current zsh session:

```console
$ source <(odoo-work-cli completion zsh)
```

Install it for every new bash session (Linux):

```console
$ odoo-work-cli completion bash > /etc/bash_completion.d/odoo-work-cli
```
